raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27066 added fast paths through varlen support to the USPAttention. This was hardcoded to either use FA (FAv3 or FAv4) or as a fallback SDPA. These calls call FA directly through the FA interface, not through the attention backends. This limits the functionality to these backends only, even when the other backend would support it (AITER on ROCm, for example). This PR changes the call so that they go through the selected attention backend instead. The backends got a new property `has_native_varlen_kernel`, which gates the usage of these fast paths to backends that support varlen natively and thus benefit from this. ## Modifications - Adds `AttentionImpl.has_native_varlen_kernel()`, defaulting to `False`. It declares whether the underlying kernel consumes `cu_seqlens` itself, as opposed to forward_varlen emulating segments with a per-segment Python loop. - `AttentionImpl.forward_varlen()` gains optional `cu_seqlens_k` / `max_seqlen_k`. Omitted, both sides use the query bounds, so every existing caller is unchanged. They exist for the K/V-gather site, where queries and keys carry different segment lengths. - Backends declaring native varlen override `has_native_varlen_kernel()` to `True` - USPAttention fast paths call sites move from a direct `flash_attn_varlen_func`call to `self.attn_impl.forward_varlen()` ## Accuracy Tests Tested on H200. ### Tail path ``` sglang generate \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 \ --height 2048 --width 2048 \ --num-inference-steps 50 \ --guidance-scale 0.0 \ --dit-cpu-offload False --dit-layerwise-offload False \ --text-encoder-cpu-offload False --image-encoder-cpu-offload False \ --offload-during-compile False --vae-cpu-offload False \ --warmup-mode request --warmup-steps 2 \ --vae-precision bf16 --image-encoder-precision bf16 \ --output-path "$OUT" --perf-dump-path "$OUT/perf.json" \ --master-port "$P" --scheduler-port "$((P+500))" \ --prompt "A cat holding a sign that says hello world" --seed 42 \ --ulysses-degree 8 --ring-degree 1 --num-gpus 8 ``` #### Before Timing: 6.40s #### After Timing: 6.39s ### KV-gather path ``` sglang generate \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 \ --height 2048 --width 2048 \ --num-inference-steps 50 \ --guidance-scale 0.0 \ --dit-cpu-offload False --dit-layerwise-offload False \ --text-encoder-cpu-offload False --image-encoder-cpu-offload False \ --offload-during-compile False --vae-cpu-offload False \ --warmup-mode request --warmup-steps 2 \ --vae-precision bf16 --image-encoder-precision bf16 \ --output-path "$OUT" --perf-dump-path "$OUT/perf.json" \ --master-port "$P" --scheduler-port "$((P+500))" \ --prompt "A cat holding a sign that says hello world" --seed 42 \ --kv-gather-degree 8 --num-gpus 8 --enable-cfg-parallel False ``` #### Before Timing: 7.51s #### After Timing: 7.52s ### Packed fast path ``` sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 --num-gpus 1 \ --batching-mode dynamic --batching-max-size 2 --batching-delay-ms 400 \ --dit-cpu-offload False --text-encoder-cpu-offload False --vae-cpu-offload False \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$P" --master-port "$((P+500))" --scheduler-port "$((P+600))" ``` ``` {"prompt": "", "width": 1024, "height": 1024, "num_inference_steps": 30, "guidance_scale": 0.0, "seed": 42, "response_format": "b64_json"} ``` #### Before Timing: 7.30s #### After Timing: 7.30s ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #38418267380](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38418267380) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #38418267004](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38418267004) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #38418266994](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38418266994)
